structured_output.world_model:
W1 (mechanism), after E009.

The setup
- The tip is E008: Muon on the conv filters, Lookahead/EMA, and resizing 24/28/32 px at 40/30/30% of steps. Batch 2000, about 238 steps. The code says epochs=9.5, and the idea texts' labels run about one epoch behind it.
- The tip scores time 6.977 s and accuracy 0.7572, so the margin over 0.753 is 0.42 pp.
- E009 timed at 6.99 s, the same as E008, so it actually ran on the 8.5-epoch tip, not on the 9-epoch E007.

Measured effects
- Compile + fused SGD: about −14% time with deterministic accuracy. E003 and E004 gave the identical 0.748633.
- Lookahead/EMA: +0.97 pp for about 0.6% time (E005). The t^3 alpha ramp acts as a strong anneal over weights and BN buffers.
- LR floor 0.07 → 0: −0.08 pp (E009), within noise. The EMA already does the annealing, so the two are redundant, not complementary. H1.3.4 is refuted.
- Muon on the conv filters: +0.66 pp at +4% time (E006).
- Progressive resizing: −22% time, −0.59 pp (E007). Time tracks pixel share, so the run is GPU/FLOP-bound.
- Epoch slope with EMA and Muon on: 0.5 epoch = −0.18 pp and −4.8% time (E008).
- Without EMA, the slope was about 0.33 pp per 0.5 epoch (E001→E002). EMA flattens the curve.

The time model
- Fixed cost is about 0.4 s: H2D copy, eigh, pad, per-epoch augment and interpolate.
- The variable part, about 6.6 s, scales with the pixel share (0.755 now).
- FLOP split by group at 32 px: about 20/48/32%. Narrowing group 3 from 576 to 512 cuts about 4.7% of conv FLOPs and some of the Muon Newton-Schulz cost. Small maps run inefficiently, so the time saving should be about 3-5%.
- At about 27 ms per step the GPU is saturated. There are no host syncs per step: the LR fill_ and the alpha lookup are CPU floats. CPU launch latency is therefore hidden, and CUDA graphs can gain only about 0-3%.

The accuracy model
- My bias: I have underestimated accuracy in 4 of 8 forecasts (E003, E005, E006, E007). This recipe family holds up better than my priors, so I shade accuracy up by about 0.2 pp.
- Further pixel cuts: the 20 px phase leaves group-3 maps at 2×2 and shrinks the 32 px tail to 20%. I expect −0.4 to −0.9 pp, which likely lands near or below 0.753.
- Per unit of time saved, resizing and epoch cuts cost about the same accuracy: roughly 0.35-0.5 pp per 10% of time.
- Width 512: on 100 classes the last group carries the class features. I expect −0.1 to −0.35 pp.

Noise
- Accuracy is bit-identical on re-runs. Time varies by about 1-2% between runs.
- Seed std is about 0.2-0.3 pp per seed, so the 3-seed mean std is about 0.15 pp.
- Keep the 3-seed mean at 0.755 or above for 40-seed safety.

Unsure
- How nonlinear the low-resolution penalty is once the 32 px tail drops below 30%.
- Whether the flat EMA-era slope (0.18 pp per 0.5 epoch) holds below 8.5 epochs.
- Whether combining width 512 with an epoch trim beats more resizing.

forecasts.reason: The pixel share drops from 0.755 to 0.639 (about −12% time), but the 20 px phase and the shorter 32 px tail cost about 0.5-0.7 pp. That is roughly the same trade as an epoch cut and likely lands at the bar.
Group 3 is about 32% of FLOPs and the change cuts about 4.7% of them, so time drops about 3-5%, right at the 4% threshold. The accuracy loss of about 0.2 pp also sits near the 0.3 pp limit.
The recipe is unchanged and deterministic, so the official seeds 0-2 repeat E008. Over 10 held-out seeds the mean should land within 0.3 pp and the std near 0.2-0.3.
The run is GPU-bound at about 27 ms per step with no host syncs, so launch overhead is already hidden. Graphs give at most about 1-3%, and re-autotuned kernels may slightly reshuffle accuracy.

cruxes: Is the accuracy cost of low resolution linear in pixel share, or does it get worse once group-3 maps reach 2×2 at 20 px? This decides whether to go deeper on resizing or cut epochs instead.
Does the flat EMA-era epoch slope (about 0.18 pp per 0.5 epoch) hold below 8.5 epochs? If it does, epoch trims are the cheapest way to spend the remaining 0.42 pp margin.
What do held-out seeds give for std and offset? This sets how close to 0.753 the 3-seed mean can safely sit.
